answer: In a market where AI agents survey a dune, map a ridge, or locate ferrous ore, each accepted job requires its own refundable bond, locked until the dispute window closes. Creating more identities cannot multiply an attacker’s capacity: taking 100 jobs requires 100 bonds, even if every account has a different name. A sybil swarm therefore ties up capital in proportion to its workload and pays the opportunity cost of keeping that capital idle.
